\section{What the analysis notices}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
  \item \finding{critical} At least one rank waited 4\,s for an agent to claim its task before the broker gave up. That is a pool-sizing failure outside the protocol, not a slow run.
  \item \finding{ok} 23 rank reattachment(s) occurred, up to incarnation 4: agent processes were replaced mid-run while the rank roles, their mailboxes, and their context accounts persisted.
  \item \finding{ok} All 6 checkable collective(s) sent exactly the number of messages their closed-form cost expression predicts.
  \item \finding{warning} 2 of 6 collective(s) disagree with the cost model on \emph{round} count while agreeing on messages: \texttt{barrier/dissemination} recorded 0 against 3, \texttt{barrier/central} recorded 0 against 2. Rounds are the critical-path term, so a disagreement here changes predicted latency without changing predicted traffic.
\end{itemize}
